name: Neogen Chemicals Ltd
tagline: A battery-electrolyte optionality bet undermined by repeated capacity delays and heavy reliance on a struggling anchor customer
business_overview: Neogen Chemicals is a specialty-chemicals manufacturer (bromine derivatives, lithium salts) expanding into lithium-ion battery electrolytes and electrolyte salts (LiPF6) via a JV with Morita (Japan), targeting India's nascent EV battery supply chain.
fundamentals_table: May 2026 community read: 'Another delay in Dahej and Pakhajan. Circuit down on Monday!' - stock hit lower circuit on renewed capacity-timeline slippage
Rs 966.70 - 2,374.00 (stock down >50% from highs per a Dec 2025 community post)
fundamentals_narrative: Weak trailing returns (ROE under 5%, ROCE under 7%) despite decent historical top-line growth, and the forward-looking battery-electrolyte optionality thesis - the main reason to hold this stock - has been repeatedly undermined by capacity-ramp delays at the Dahej and Pakhajan plants.
sentiment_summary: Read the most recent 50 of 91 available posts (Jan 2022-May 2026). Sentiment turned decisively bearish from Dec 2025 onward: a detailed bull case (Morita JV optionality) was published, immediately followed by substantive pushback questioning the underlying PAT-margin assumptions and customer-concentration risk, and the thread's most recent post (May 2026) reports a fresh capacity delay and a lower-circuit stock reaction.
community_signal: No VP-trusted-tier user posted in the read window. naveendahiya (non-trusted) argued in Dec 2025 that the market was under-pricing the Morita JV battery-electrolyte optionality following a >50% stock correction. HBORA1012 (non-trusted) pushed back with detailed margin-assumption math questioning whether 9% PAT margins are achievable given Rs 225-250 Cr of expected depreciation+interest costs. garg.saurabh1975 (non-trusted) flagged that Neogen's electrolyte ramp is heavily dependent on Ola Electric's giga-factory, which was itself reported to be facing a 'serious meltdown.' The thread's final post (May 2026, Gsa1704) reports yet another delay at both the Dahej and Pakhajan plants, with the stock hitting a lower circuit.
bull_case: Genuine large-market optionality: India's nascent EV battery-electrolyte/lithium-salt supply chain localisation, with named target customers including Reliance, Tata Group, Exide, Amara Raja, Ola Electric, and Waaree
Stock is down more than 50% from its highs, potentially pricing in most of the bad news already
Decent historical 10-year median revenue growth of 20.3%
bear_case: Repeated, compounding capacity-ramp delays at both the Dahej and Pakhajan plants, with the most recent (May 2026) delay triggering a lower-circuit stock move - a pattern of execution failure, not a one-off
Heavy customer-concentration risk on Ola Electric's giga-factory ramp, which a community member described as facing a 'serious meltdown'
Weak trailing profitability (ROE under 5%, ROCE under 7%) combined with elevated debt (D/E 1.63) leaves little margin for further delays

A detailed community pushback (Dec 2025) directly challenges whether the bull case's PAT-margin assumptions (9%) are achievable given the company's own disclosed peak depreciation/interest cost structure
verdict_headline: Optionality thesis undermined by a repeated pattern of execution delays and a shaky anchor customer
verdict_reasoning: Both the trailing (weak ROE/ROCE, elevated debt) and the recent-trend (repeated delays, lower-circuit move in May 2026) pictures are weak here - this does not meet the bar for the project's 'recent-quarter inflection' exception

The one real catalyst (battery-electrolyte optionality) is credible in size but has consistently failed to materialise on schedule across multiple plants and quarters, and depends heavily on a customer (Ola Electric) reported to be in its own distress
Conviction kept Low pending evidence that the Dahej/Pakhajan capacity actually comes online and ships to a stable customer base

four_box.note: Verdict explicit: battery-electrolyte optionality 'has consistently failed to materialise on schedule across multiple plants and quarters' and depends on Ola Electric, itself 'reported to be in its own distress' (tailwind weak); trailing ROE/ROCE weak, elevated debt.
